sovereignty: Supreme authority of the state, vested in the people of Nepal
fundamental rights: Basic human rights guaranteed by the Constitution that cannot be suspended
directive principles: Guidelines for the state to follow when making laws — not enforceable by courts
federalism: Division of power between federal, provincial, and local governments
secularism: State treats all religions equally; no official state religion
inclusive: Ensuring representation of women, Dalits, indigenous peoples, Madhesis, Tharus, Muslims, and minorities
proportional representation: Electoral system where seats match the percentage of votes each party receives
impeachment: Process to remove high officials (President, judges) for violating the Constitution
judicial review: Power of courts to strike down laws that violate the Constitution
habeas corpus: Court order requiring a person under arrest to be brought before a judge
citizenship: Legal status of being a member of the Nepali state with rights and duties
constituent assembly: Body elected to write the Constitution (dissolved after promulgation)
promulgation: Official publication and enactment of the Constitution (September 20, 2015)
amendment: Formal change to the Constitution requiring two-thirds majority in Parliament
emergency powers: Special powers for the executive during crisis (Article 273–275)
state of emergency: Declared when sovereignty, territorial integrity, or security is threatened
parliament: Federal legislature consisting of House of Representatives and National Assembly
cabinet: Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister — executive authority
vote of confidence: Parliamentary test whether the government retains majority support
ordinance: Temporary law issued by the President on Cabinet recommendation when Parliament is not in session
finance bill: Bill concerning taxation, borrowing, or expenditure — only House of Representatives can originate
money bill: Bill exclusively about taxation, public money, or loans — special procedure applies
public service commission: Independent body for fair recruitment to civil service (Article 243)
auditor general: Independent auditor of all government accounts (Article 241)
cooperative federalism: Federal, provincial, and local governments working together collaboratively
residual powers: Powers not listed in federal, provincial, or concurrent lists — remain with federation
